text.title: Futures mixed after tech rout as Nvidia earnings loom; Home Depot weighs on Dow
text.summary: US stocks fell sharply Monday, with the Nasdaq down 2.5% and the S&P 500 down 1.9%. Futures are mixed this morning: Nasdaq 100 is up 0.4%, the S&P 500 is flat and the Dow is down 0.6%. Attention is on Nvidia's results after the close and on 8:30 AM retail sales data.

drivers.t: Nvidia shares pulled back 4.1% as traders sold ahead of its report due after the bell, and options are pricing in a bigger-than-usual move. Co-founder Jensen Huang's departure is also on investors' minds.

Washington China hawks are pushing new tech restrictions that could test the US-China trade truce, and a Trump China data center curb is reportedly advancing. Nvidia has formed a board committee on national security and export controls.
Nasdaq 100 futures are higher as selling pressure on tech eased ahead of Nvidia's report. A fund manager survey showed tech bets cut at the fastest pace in two decades.
Dow futures are down about 0.6%, with Home Depot cited as a weight. The stock is down 1.9% pre-market after the company named a new CEO.

Japan fell 1.3% and the major European indexes are down roughly 1%, with Deutsche Bank shares dropping on a leak report. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped 3 bp to 5.12% and the 2-year slipped 5 bp to 4.83%, even as Fed's Musalem said several rate hikes are likely needed by spring.

earnings.t: Home Depot named Richard McPhail as its new CEO, effective next week, alongside the quarterly report.
Disney is targeting $3 billion in savings through cost-cutting, and investors want more detail on CEO Josh D'Amaro's strategy after several rounds of layoffs.

Nike investor day at its Oregon headquarters, its first in nine years
